index.faq.q7: Do I need IGETC or Cal-GETC to transfer to UC?
index.faq.a7: No. Neither is an admission requirement. UC asks for a seven-course pattern by the end of the spring term before you transfer: two English composition courses, one math or quantitative reasoning course, and four courses from at least two of arts and humanities, social and behavioral sciences, and physical and biological sciences — all UC-transferable. You also need 60 semester units and a 2.4 GPA in UC-transferable courses (2.8 if you are a nonresident). If you finish IGETC or Cal-GETC you may already have met the seven-course pattern, and some majors recommend it, so check ASSIST and your transfer center.
index.faq.a7link: UC Admissions: basic requirements and the seven-course pattern
index.faq.q8: How much is the UC application? Is there a fee waiver?
index.faq.a8: $80 per UC campus ($95 for international and non-immigrant applicants). UC waives the fee for up to four campuses for eligible U.S. citizens, permanent residents and AB 540 students; the application tells you whether you qualify once you enter family size and income. Fees are not refundable.
index.faq.a8link: UC Admissions: application fees and waivers
index.faq.q9: What about financial aid (FAFSA or Dream Act)?
index.faq.a9: File the 2027–28 FAFSA, or the California Dream Act Application if you are an undocumented student, between October 1, 2026 and March 2, 2027. California residents (and AB 540 students) also need a Cal Grant GPA verification; California community colleges usually submit it for you, but check with your school.
index.faq.q10: Can I transfer in winter or spring?
index.faq.a10: Most UC campuses admit transfer students for fall only. Select campuses accept winter/spring applications in a July filing period (July 1–31 for winter/spring 2027). Not every campus or major is open, so check the campus before you apply. TAG for winter/spring has its own filing period, May 1–31.
index.faq.q11: Who should I talk to about my own plan?
index.faq.a11: Your community college transfer center or counselor. They know your college’s ASSIST agreements and deadlines, and they can review your plan with you. UCPlan does not give personal transfer advising.
cuc.who.title: Who it is for
cuc.who.p: Students who are already at UC Irvine, UC San Diego or UC Santa Barbara. Its first question is whether you are aiming for grad school or a job; then it plans your semesters against your graduation requirements. It is not a transfer planner — if you are still at a community college, start with Transfer-OS.
